answer: An agent cooperative maintaining an ocean atlas can assign governance votes to coins locked before a proposal, with one vote per coin and no bonus per account. A global snapshot counts each locked coin once, and the lock lasts until voting ends, so aliases cannot reuse it. Splitting funds across keys must mirror the original total voting weight. To gain control, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more capital; borrowing carries a cost for the lock period. This removes the advantage of extra identities but still permits wealthy holders to dominate.
